stories.body: Right-wing senator Flávio Bolsonaro won the first round of Brazil’s presidential election with about 47% of the vote, ahead of President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva’s roughly 45%, but short of the majority needed to avoid a runoff. The two will face each other on 25 October in a contest that could return the Bolsonaro political movement to power while former president Jair Bolsonaro serves a prison sentence for plotting a coup after his 2022 defeat. Bolsonaro’s stronger-than-expected result, alongside gains for right-wing candidates in congressional and gubernatorial races, makes him a formidable contender as supporters of eliminated candidates decide where to direct their votes.
stories.headline: Brazil election heads to runoff as Flávio Bolsonaro leads Lula in first round

stories.body: Yemen’s internationally recognised, Saudi-backed government has announced a military campaign to retake all territory held by the Iran-aligned Houthis, escalating fighting that has intensified after years of relative stalemate. Government forces said they had regained the coastal Dhubab district and were beginning an offensive toward Houthi-held Sanaa, though the Houthis disputed some claims. The push follows recent Houthi advances along the Red Sea coast and around Taiz, including the reported cutting of a vital route to the besieged city; fighting has killed scores of combatants and renewed fears of a wider humanitarian crisis.
stories.headline: Yemen’s Saudi-backed government launches offensive against Houthi-held territory

stories.body: Ethiopian federal forces and allied fighters have taken control of Mekelle after the Tigray People’s Liberation Front said it had temporarily withdrawn from the regional capital to reduce risks to civilians. The development marks a major escalation in renewed fighting across Tigray and nearby regions, less than four years after the Pretoria agreement ended a devastating two-year war. The TPLF says the peace deal has effectively collapsed, while the federal government says it remains committed to it; the renewed conflict has raised fears of fresh displacement, economic damage and wider regional instability.
stories.headline: Ethiopian forces retake Mekelle as fighting resumes in Tigray

stories.body: The United States has withdrawn its B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford in Britain, where counterterrorism police are investigating suspicious activity near the base and reports of a possible Iran-backed plot. Six men have been arrested and released on bail in connection with the inquiry, while Iranian authorities have denied involvement. The base has recently supported US operations connected to Iran, and British officials say the threat from Iran remains high; the bomber withdrawal was described as an operational military decision rather than a political one.
stories.headline: US withdraws B-1 bombers from RAF Fairford after suspected terror threat

stories.body: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel have been awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries underlying optogenetics, a technique that uses light-sensitive proteins to control the electrical activity of cells. Their work has allowed researchers to switch specific neural circuits on and off in animal studies, greatly expanding the ability to investigate memory, behaviour and neurological or psychiatric disorders. The approach is also being explored clinically, including efforts to restore limited vision in people with retinal disease.
stories.headline: Nobel Prize in Medicine awarded for work enabling control of neurons with light

stories.body: Investigators believe the co-pilot accused of attacking the captain of a Flydubai flight from Dubai to Tel Aviv planned to crash the Boeing 737 MAX into Ben Gurion airport or a building in central Tel Aviv. The Omani national allegedly used an emergency cockpit axe to wound the captain before passengers and crew overpowered him; the plane made an emergency landing in Saudi Arabia. Reports say he may have acted alone, though the investigation is continuing, and scrutiny has focused on how he was hired after reportedly being barred from flying by Oman Air over concerns about extremist views.
stories.headline: Flydubai co-pilot accused of planning to crash aircraft in Tel Aviv

stories.body: The US Supreme Court opens a new term facing consequential cases involving religion, elections and immigration. The court’s agenda will be watched closely for rulings that could shape federal power and electoral rules, as well as for signs of whether a justice may retire and create a vacancy with major political implications.
stories.headline: Supreme Court begins term with major cases on religion, elections and immigration ahead

stories.body: Thousands of public servants seeking federal student-loan forgiveness are facing extended delays as a program intended to help borrowers catch up on payments falls behind. Staffing cuts and a surge in applications have slowed processing, leaving borrowers who expected relief after years of qualifying public-sector work waiting for decisions.
stories.headline: Public servants face long waits for student-loan forgiveness

stories.body: New NBC News/Telemundo and CBS News/YouGov polling shows Latino voters favouring Democratic congressional candidates by wide margins ahead of the midterms, threatening Republican gains with the group in 2024. Economic pressure, high living costs and dissatisfaction with President Donald Trump’s immigration enforcement appear to be driving the shift: most respondents disapprove of his handling of the economy and say his immigration policies have gone too far. The findings do not indicate broad enthusiasm for Democrats, whose favourability among Latino voters remains closely divided.
stories.headline: Polls show Latino voters shifting toward Democrats ahead of midterms

stories.body: Texas Senate candidate Ken Paxton privately told donors that he has little control over his campaign’s messaging because decisions in a federal race are coming from Washington, according to recordings reported by Politico. The remarks sit awkwardly with Paxton’s prior attacks on rivals as Washington insiders and come as he trails Democratic challenger James Talarico in a recent New York Times/Siena poll. A campaign adviser said Paxton was referring to independent super PAC activity, which campaigns are legally barred from coordinating with.
stories.headline: Ken Paxton says Washington is driving his Texas Senate campaign message

stories.body: Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez has called an early general election for 29 November after his government lost two housing decrees in Congress, exposing the fragility of its parliamentary support. Sánchez argued that Spain needs a broader progressive majority to continue pursuing housing and social policies, while highlighting his government’s economic record and attacking the opposition’s obstruction. The campaign is expected to focus heavily on housing affordability and evictions after recent public protests over the issue.
stories.headline: Pedro Sánchez calls Spain’s general election for 29 November

stories.body: After calling the election and dissolving parliament, Spain’s government plans to approve revised versions of housing measures rejected by Congress and submit them to the lower house’s permanent committee for ratification. The smaller body has a different balance of seats, meaning the government could pass an anti-eviction measure without support from Junts if other allies, including the Basque Nationalist Party, back it. The government is considering changes to the texts to avoid legal objections to resubmitting decrees that the full Congress recently rejected.
stories.headline: Spanish government seeks to revive housing measures through parliamentary standing committee

stories.body: Fresh torrential rain has brought flooding and major transport disruption across Barcelona and surrounding parts of Catalunya, prompting civil-protection alerts urging people to avoid travel, basements, rivers and flood-prone areas. Authorities reported cancelled flights at Barcelona-El Prat, disruptions to Metro and Rodalies services, and flooded roads after rainfall that officials said exceeded forecasts. The episode follows a severe weekend of storms that left two people dead, with new warnings issued in coastal areas over rising river and stream levels.
stories.headline: Torrential rain and flooding disrupt transport across Barcelona and Catalunya

stories.body: A new line of storms has dropped close to or more than 100 litres of rain per square metre in parts of Barcelona, with especially heavy totals in northern and hillside neighbourhoods. Combined with earlier rain, some locations have recorded more than 320 litres in the past week, exceeding half of the city’s usual annual rainfall. At the Fabra Observatory, rainfall in the first days of October has already surpassed three times the monthly average, making this Barcelona’s wettest October since 1987 with most of the month still to come.
stories.headline: Barcelona’s latest downpour makes this its wettest October in nearly four decades

stories.body: Torrential rain has flooded facilities at several Barcelona schools, forcing some pupils to eat in classrooms while damaged dining rooms, kitchens, gyms and playgrounds are assessed. At Escola Poeta Foix in Putxet, water entered the semi-basement dining area, while other centres reported flooded sports areas, leaks and damaged materials. At Poeta Foix, families said a burst external wastewater pipe sent water knee-deep into parts of the school; education officials said they were compiling incidents and sending technical staff to assess the damage.
stories.headline: Flooding damages Barcelona schools and disrupts meals and classes
